findings.claim_strength: No statistically supported downstream assignment benefit; absence or equivalence is not established.
findings.qualification: Assigned/control consideration pairs: N=966/1015, weighted N=973.61/1000.17, ESS=839.32/877.62; usage pairs: N=969/1007, weighted N=973.30/993.81, ESS=842.04/868.83. Each arm began with 1400 eligible households. Control growth cannot be assigned to a particular secular mechanism.

findings.proposition: Attrition materially limits interpretation: 1019 assigned and 1070 control households returned, with weighted return rates of 72.38% and 75.98%. Returners had higher baseline consideration (30.13% versus 21.99%), higher digital confidence (46.34% versus 36.56%), and lower high budget pressure (33.68% versus 49.20%) than nonreturners.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive evidence of selective follow-up; direction and size of resulting outcome bias remain unknown.
findings.qualification: Return-status denominators are all 1400 households per arm. Exact eligible/valid N, weighted N and ESS for all six baseline profiles are retained in attrition_audit. Arm differences also existed before attrition: consideration was 29.79% control versus 26.31% assigned, and 31.48% versus 28.76% among returners. These comparisons neither invalidate randomisation nor establish ignorable missingness.

findings.proposition: Large recipient and recaller consideration gaps should not be sold as campaign lift. Logged recipients led nonrecipients by 19.12 points at follow-up, but already led by 19.15 at baseline. Recallers led by 37.24 points at follow-up and 32.35 at baseline.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive association with substantial pre-existing differences, not a causal receipt or recall effect.
findings.qualification: Receipt/no-receipt pair bases: N=1037/944, weighted N=970.04/1003.75, ESS=903.73/820.43. Recall/no-recall bases: N=844/1040, weighted N=760.65/1107.13, ESS=741.87/906.03; 97 consideration pairs lack valid recall. Each comparison uses the same people at both waves. Recall was measured after outcomes.

findings.proposition: Assignment changed the observed delivery environment without creating clean exposed and unexposed groups: logged receipt was 70.16% assigned versus 24.54% control; recall was 48.61% versus 32.97%. Among returned valid-recall respondents, 65.82% of logged recipients recalled the campaign, while 15.73% without a logged receipt also recalled it.
findings.qualification: Receipt uses all enrolled households; recall uses only valid answers among returners. Exact bases and exclusions are in receipt_recall_and_selection. Logged receipt is not proven attention, recall is not verified exposure, and neither should replace assignment in the primary analysis.

findings.proposition: Households with children have a stronger observed need, but superior campaign responsiveness is unestablished. Very/extremely stressful meal planning was reported by 56.48% with children versus 36.56% without. Children-household assignment contrasts were +10.15 points awareness, +2.95 consideration and +0.91 usage; none of the children-versus-no-children interactions survived Holm adjustment.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive audience need; no supported differential response in the prespecified interaction family.
findings.qualification: Stress valid N=1060 with children and 1686 without; weighted N=950.38/1791.67, ESS=958.69/1451.12. Interaction estimates were −5.07 awareness, +4.27 consideration and +2.81 usage points; respective 95% CIs were [−13.46,3.32], [−2.95,11.48], [−0.98,6.59], with Holm p=.472/.472/.438. Four-cell eligible and paired bases are in children_need_and_heterogeneity. Numerical subgroup leads do not establish targeting superiority.

findings.proposition: Selected recallers generally rated the message positively: agreement was 76.74% for clarity, 75.90% for believability and 70.52% for relevance. Relevance is a reasonable creative-test hypothesis, but its numerical ranking does not prove it is weaker or that improving it would increase usage.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive diagnostic evidence supporting a test hypothesis only.
findings.qualification: Eligible recallers N=891, weighted N=800.64, ESS=781.76; valid item N=852–862. Full distributions and exact bases are retained in selected_recaller_diagnostics. Pairwise correlations of .504–.544 describe shared ratings, not independent causal drivers; nonrecallers were not asked.

findings.proposition: The evidence supports a further controlled test with an explicit awareness objective and a separately powered downstream question; it does not yet support a sales, ROI or superior-targeting claim. Improve follow-up retention, prespecify a meaningful consideration/use threshold, and retain households with children as a planned audience rather than declaring them campaign winners.
findings.claim_strength: Research recommendation inferred from the supported awareness result, downstream uncertainty and follow-up limitations.
findings.qualification: This is a recommendation to learn, not proof of commercial value. Consideration is not purchasing and reported usage is not verified activity or sales; costs and revenue are absent. The exploratory older, digitally confident online-grocery subgroup has only 22 control and 21 assigned pairs: insufficient base, with all outcome estimates suppressed.
